paragraphs.text: Good evening, elders and sisters. We hope you have really enjoyed your Sabbath day-to-day. Sister Hughes and I had the blessing of sharing the sacrament ordinance with sisters Ordesta, Sy, and Aldea up in the Bocaue area. We're grateful for them and for all of you. What a blessed day it's been.
I have just a couple of updates for you.

First, the area of presidency has asked that when you go out to do your shopping, regardless of what day that is, that you wear your preparation day clothes with your name tag where it can be easily seen. They want you to be neat and well-dressed, but just not in missionary attire. This is really more for the elders because the white shirt and tie really causes them to stand out.

This is just a safety consideration, so use good judgment and common sense. You don't need to be alarmed or take any great change in what you're doing. Don't make yourself stand out quite so much from a distance, if you know what I mean.

We still have three of our missionaries at the MTC, Sister Javed, Sister Salatielu, and Elder Tawa. They have not been able to get travel arranged back to their home countries. We're praying that they will soon be able to travel home or at least come back to us in the mission. All three of them are trying to get back to the mission, so remember them in your prayers, please.

Now, I'm looking forward to zone interviews, which will start tomorrow afternoon. Please try to arrange the situation on your side of the video call such that you have privacy and can talk with me openly about what's on your mind and how I might be able to help you in your ministry, your mission, your service.

Now to the message that has been on my mind for the past few days. It seems a little strange that I should be thinking about this set of verses when we're here on lockdown, but I'm sure the Lord has a reason for bringing this to my mind. And maybe as you ponder what I'm going to share, he will bring something to your mind that will be helpful to you in your mission and ministry.

With just seven short verses in section 4 of the Doctrine and Covenants, the Lord tells us pretty much everything we need to know about missionary work. He tells us the condition of the world, i.e. the field is wide already to harvest. And more importantly, he tells us what our condition needs to be in order for us to be successful in the,
Verse one,
Section four was given in February of 1829, so just about 14 months before the church was even organized, truly the marvelous work was about to come forth.
Verse two,

Now each of us has embarked in the service of God. Are we serving him with all our heart, might, mind, and strength? The promised blessing for those that do is wonderful and something I would think all of us would desire with all of our hearts.
Verse three,

As you remember, elders and sisters, you truly desired to serve God. You sought this calling as a missionary. You worked hard to qualify, to make it through the application process, the interview process, the medicals and dental examinations, and all the different things that you had to do to qualify to come on a mission. Because of your desires and the statements of conviction that you made to serve faithfully, you were called to the work.
So verse four,

We are told by the Lord himself that the time is now, the harvest is here and ready. We are here to baptize converts. If we do, we bring salvation to our own soul. With that kind of promise, why would we waste a single minute of the Lord's time?

It is so disappointing to me to see missionaries standing around and just using time poorly when they should be working, working in some way, even in the lockdown, working in our self-development project, working in our online ministry, working in ways to uplift and build up others, our missionary colleagues, the members, non-members, and so forth.

I invite each of you to recommit yourself to do what you originally agreed to do before you got your call. Be a person of your word, be a person of integrity. The world is full of talkers, but there are very few, very, very few indeed, doers. You want to be a doer of the word and not a hearer or a talker only.
Verse 5,
These are some of the attributes of Christ combined with the focus on Christ that is so essential for the disciple of Christ. These are attributes that qualify you for the work.
Verse 6,

We are here reminded again of these necessary attributes. You're probably finding how necessary they are being confined to the apartment all day with the same missionaries. You need to have these attributes so that there will be love in the apartment and a spirit of well-being and an edifying sense between the two of you, the three of you, the four of you, the five of you, the six of you in that apartment.

As you exercise, these attributes found in verse 6, what happens is your whole group of missionaries in that apartment will grow together in the Lord, giving yourselves power to help one another and build each other up so that you become better in your missionary service. We are absolutely, and this is key, you are absolutely trying to build these in a season of your life that will allow you to own these attributes for the rest of your life.

Now it's interesting, the last attribute is listed as diligence, and I wonder if the Lord placed it last so that it would be the one we remembered the most. In my business career, I have been astonished by how lazy most people choose to be. They give a half-hearted effort and then wonder why they don't keep their job or they don't have the respect of their peers or they don't get paid as much as they want to get paid. Being diligent is a sign of self-respect. People who respect themselves don't waste their time, and they certainly don't waste God's time.
As I write these words, I'm reminded of the words of President Ezra Taft Benson, spoken to a group of missionaries back in 1988 and reprinted in Preach My Gospel on page 121. Quote,
close quote.
Now verse seven,

In this final verse, the Lord counsels us to make the necessary effort to seek his assistance in all we do. He promises us that if we ask, if we will receive, if we knock, the way will be opened before us. I sincerely pray that each of you will do a self-inventory and ask the Lord to help you rise up and become a better, more effective version of yourself.

I promise you that you will never regret the days you worked hard in the mission, especially the days when it wasn't easy, the days when we were confined to the apartment. Finding ways to be proactively engaged in the work of the Lord in this strange season we're in will be more powerful for you than any other season of your mission. But you will become incredibly bitterly regretful of those days when you chose to waste the Lord's time. You'll remember those days.

So renew your commitment right now to serve with all your heart from this day until the moment you receive your honorable release. I signed about 30 honorable release certificates just today that will be mailed to missionaries whose missions were cut short. I've heard from many of these missionaries about how unsatisfactory the feeling was to be in the thick of their mission going for it, really feeling great about their service and then within a matter of hours being out of it and how disappointed they are.

Now we have no control over that sort of thing, but you can make advantage every day of your mission right now and you can choose to make each hour of each day be an hour of power for you both in the work and in your development. This kind of a commitment made and kept will create a sweetness to your mission memories and a magnetically attracting power to wonderful opportunities in your life after your mission.

We love you. We are so very proud of your mental toughness and your spiritual resilience. You are showing yourselves to be the remarkable generation that you've been spoken of by prophets in our modern day. Keep it going. Don't be tempted to fall off the path just because you got yourself bored. Choose to be active. Choose to be engaged. Choose to be innovative. Rest well elders and sisters and make tomorrow a great day by choice.
